commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Retain encoder cache references for repeated multimodal inputs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Prevent premature encoder-cache eviction when repeated multimodal inputs are deduplicated within the same scheduling step. 

## Claims

- Preserve cache references for partially consumed duplicate inputs, including locally encoded and externally loaded inputs.
- Avoid unnecessary re-encoding and scheduling stalls caused by premature eviction.
- Register duplicate occurrences within the final scheduled window, including the existing prefill lookahead, without registering later occurrences outside that window.

## Validation

On upstream base `d61081dc3d`, using the existing development environment:

```bash
uv run --no-project --python /workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -q
```

Result: **241 passed, 2 failed**.

Both failures require multiple GPUs and also fail on the unchanged upstream base in the same single-GPU environment:

- `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`
- `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait`

The new parameterized regression test covers newly admitted and running requests, with local encoding and external cache loads. All four cases pass. It verifies that:

- a competing request cannot evict an input that still has a partially consumed duplicate;
- no additional local encoding is scheduled; and
- later unscheduled occurrences are not registered as references.

Pre-commit checks pass.

Model end-to-end validation and latency measurements have not been performed, so no measured performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

Same-step deduplication allocates cache space only for the first occurrence of an input. Later occurrences within the same scheduling window reuse that entry but are not registered as references.

Once the first occurrence is consumed, the cache manager can therefore consider the entry reclaimable even though another occurrence is still partially consumed. A competing request can then evict the entry prematurely.

After scheduling is finalized, register cached occurrences overlapping the final scheduled window before advancing request progress. This reuses the existing reference-tracking mechanism without allocating additional cache space or scheduling duplicate encoder work.

The additional work is a window lookup and reference updates for overlapping inputs on scheduled requests that already hold encoder-cache references. Encoder-decoder models retain their existing behavior.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Run the prefill token scoring test under batch invariance
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption`, added in #56984, fails on every run ([CI #92838](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92838/list?sid=01a10aa7-6459-497e-b369-4653327ae8d8&tab=output)). Its `atol=1e-2` cross-run check cannot hold under the default kernels, so this runs the test with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and keeps the tolerance as is.

## Claims

- The test passes 10 out of 10 runs, having failed on every run before.
- The strict `atol=1e-2` is kept, so the check is not weakened.
- The feature under test is correct; the failure is tolerance, not scoring.
- Cost is 8 seconds on a 49 second test, almost all of it one-off warmup.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption
```

Cost, four alternating runs each:

| | default | batch invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| whole test | 49.0s | 57.0s |
| the 34 `generate` calls alone | 0.225s | 0.380s |

## Details

The check compares a second `generate` call against the first at `atol=1e-2`, on values around -15, so it asks two runs to agree to better than one part in a thousand. Kernel selection varies between processes, the two runs reduce in a different order, and bf16 logprob tails move by up to 0.2. The deviations recur as the same few values across runs, which is what picking between kernel variants looks like. This is the known non-determinism tracked in #27433.

Batch invariance costs this test nothing it was written to cover, because row alignment does not depend on kernel selection, and the `-inf` padding is still compared exactly.

The alternative was `rtol=0.1, atol=0.2`, which the same test already uses twenty lines below. It passes 9 runs out of 9 and saves the 8 seconds, but it weakens the check, so I kept the strict bound.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Preserve literal values in Guidance disable_additional_properties
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58695.

When `StructuredOutputsConfig.disable_additional_properties=True` is enabled for the Guidance structured-output backend, `process_for_additional_properties()` previously walked all nested dictionary and list values indiscriminately via `_walk_json_for_additional_properties()`. As a result:
1. Object literals inside `const`, `enum`, `default`, or `examples` that happened to contain a `"properties"` or `"patternProperties"` key (e.g., GeoJSON Features) had `"additionalProperties": false` injected into the literal value, causing the compiled `llguidance` matcher to reject the valid literal value and accept the mutated one instead.
2. Property maps containing a property named `"properties"` or `"patternProperties"` also had `"additionalProperties": false` injected directly into the `properties` map.

This PR updates `_walk_json_for_additional_properties()` in `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_guidance.py` to recurse only into schema-bearing keywords (`_SCHEMA_MAP_KEYWORDS` and `_SUBSCHEMA_KEYWORDS`), preserving literal instance values (`const`, `enum`, `default`, `examples`) and property maps unchanged.

### Duplicate Check

commits.pr_title: [Model][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support DCP for the kpool sparse indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot run with decode context parallelism. Its kpool sparse indexer compresses the indexer KV (`index_kpool=4`), and the indexer metadata builder rejects DCP whenever `compress_ratio > 1`. This check does not depend on the platform or the attention backend:

```
NotImplementedError: DCP is not supported with sparse indexer KV compression (compress_ratio=4)
```

This PR shards the kpool indexer across DCP ranks by pool:

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` must be a multiple of `index_kpool` (e.g. 4), so each compressed pool lives entirely on one rank. The builder now raises a clear error when this does not hold.
- `CompressedSlotMappingKernel` is DCP-aware. Each rank writes only the compressed states it owns, at rank-local positions. Prefill chunk metadata uses the interleave measured in compressed units.
- Each rank scores its local pools, takes a local top-k, and merges it across ranks with the existing DSA DCP global top-k merge (`_merge_dcp_topk_global`), using the interleave in pool units. The result is global token ids, which the sparse MLA backend already filters and localizes under DCP.
- The CuteDSL DCP merge warmup keys use pool-level top-k and interleave for kpool models.
- The raw kpool tail ring (`KpoolTailSpec`) stays replicated on every DCP rank, like Mamba state. Its pages are self-addressed (`uses_slot_mapping=False`), so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` no longer treats it as a replicated draft group that requires a block-outer layout.
- Unchanged: DeepSeek-V4 compressed KV stays unsupported under DCP, and ROCm kpool raises explicitly.

## Repro

On `main`, this fails at engine startup with the error above. On Blackwell, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` supports DCP; the indexer builder check applies on any platform.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8
```

With this PR, set the interleave to a multiple of `index_kpool`:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp 8 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4
```

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
    tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py \
    tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py
```

New tests:
- `test_compressed_slot_mapping_dcp_uses_rank_local_state_positions`: each DCP rank writes only its own compressed states, at rank-local slots.
- `test_dcp_replicated_kpool_tail_keeps_block_interior_layout`: a replicated kpool tail does not force a block-outer layout.

E2E: GSM8K (1319 questions) at 5, 25, 50 and 100 shots with `vllm serve` at TP8 + DCP8 + `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`, compared with TP8 alone (bf16 KV, no MTP).

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 309 passed on 1×H100. The 2 failures are `test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_*`, which need more than 1 GPU for their PP config and are unrelated to this change.
- E2E was run on 8×H100 together with a separate local SM90 attention-backend change that Hopper needs for DCP at head_dim 512 (out of scope here). I did not have Blackwell hardware to run this PR on its own.

| Config | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.911 – 0.922 |
| TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) | 0.916 |

5-shot GSM8K prompts are shorter than `index_topk` (2048 tokens), so that eval only lightly exercises the cross-rank top-k selection. To cover longer contexts, I raised the shot count. Both configs ran on the same build:

| Shots | Prompt tokens | TP8 | TP8 + DCP8 (interleave 4) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | ~650 | 0.916 | 0.913 |
| 25 | ~4.3k | 0.909 | 0.917 |
| 50 | ~8.5k | 0.920 | 0.920 |
| 100 | ~16.9k | 0.926 | 0.922 |

Accuracy matches TP8 at every length, including 100 shots (about 8× `index_topk`). Prefix caching was on, so the shared few-shot prefix is mostly a cache hit, while decode and the question chunks run the top-k selection over the full context.

## Duplicate check

I searched open PRs and issues for GLM-5.3-Flash / kpool / sparse-indexer DCP and found none that enables DCP for compressed indexer KV. #57161 reworks kpool compression and scheduling but does not touch DCP.

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed the changes and ran the tests above.

## Purpose

Extend the device-side multimodal input normalization (#50411) to Kimi K2.5 / K3, following the same patterns as in #51289 and #55389.

As Kimi K3's (checkpoint-owned) vision processor already normalizes on CPU and cannot skip it, this PR makes it use vLLM-owned `KimiK25FusedVisionProcessor`(#47416) which is numba-optimized and mathematically equivalent to the checkpoint-owned one up to chessboard backgrounding. As vllm converts every image to RGB before it reaches the processor, neither processor sees alpha and thus they must be equal. To verify the equivalence, the following unit test has been added:

The test checks the swap is a drop-in replacement: for the same RGB image, both processors must return the same `grid_thws`, the same `pixel_values`, and the same token count from `media_tokens_calculator`. The three sizes hit each branch of `navit_resize_image`:

| 7300×30 | exceeds `patch_limit_on_one_side`: resized, then padded |
| 13×9 | smaller than one patch: padded to a single token |

commits.pr_title: [Attention][MLA] Support fp8_ds_mla KV cache for NoPE-512 models on SM90
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This supersedes #55543 by @Leoyzen, who is kept as co-author. It enables the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM90 for rope-free sparse-MLA models with head_size 512, such as GLM-5.3-Flash, through `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`.

On H100, plain `fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (with the fix from #55222) holds more tokens. FlashMLA is still clearly faster at long-context decode: up to +31% output throughput and −29% TPOT at 16k input (see the benchmarks below). The PR adds FlashMLA as an opt-in with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`. Default backend selection doesn't change.

The idea is the same as in #55543: keep the DeepSeek 656B row and leave the RoPE slot at zero. This version keeps all of the logic inside the backend.

**How it works**
- **Cache write:** nothing changes. `concat_and_cache_mla` already zero-fills the RoPE slot when `pe_dim == 0` .
- **Query:** `FlashMLASparseImpl` sets `q_head_size = kv_lora_rank + 64` for NoPE on `fp8_ds_mla`.
  - Its q workspaces are sized from `q_head_size`.
  - `forward_mqa` zero-pads the query to that width, so q_pe · 0 = 0.
  - This covers the tuple path, the mixed and prefill paths, and DCP, where the gathered query arrives unpadded.
- **Dense-MHA prefill:** the impl sets `supports_dense_mha_prefill = False` for this layout, because the dense prefill workspace is `kv_lora_rank` wide and cannot hold the 576-wide rows. The SM120 FlashInfer impl does the same.
  - #55543 left this path on, where the FA prefill backend would see a 320-wide head.
  - `AttentionImpl.supports_dense_mha_prefill` drops `ClassVar` so it can be set per instance.
- **Backend selection:**
  - `FLASHMLA_SPARSE.supports_combination` now accepts `fp8_ds_mla` for SM90 NoPE-512.

**Compared with #55543**
- Removed:
  - the global zero buffer
  - the string check on the backend name
  - the model and wrapper hooks in `mla_attention.py`, `sparse_mla_attention.py`, `mla.py` and the glm5next attention
  - the hard-coded insert index in `cuda.py`
- The test fixtures compute the fp8_ds_mla row size as `kv_lora_rank + 16 + 128`, since the RoPE slot is always present.

## Duplicate check

- #55543 is the original PR and is superseded by this one.
- #58892 changes the SM90 backend priority for bf16 NoPE; this PR is orthogonal to it.
- #55222 fixes plain `fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`. It is a different cache format and backend, and the two PRs complement each other.
- #58305 and #53969 are SM120-only.

## Benchmarks (H100, GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8)

- **FI** is `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90`, with the #55222 plan-dtype fix applied.
- **FlashMLA** is `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla` on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` (this PR).
- Both use the same code and differ only in that flag.
- MTP is off. The workload is `vllm bench serve` with random data and `--ignore-eos`.
- Prompts per run: 16 at C=1, 32 at C=8, 128 at C=32.

**Long context: 16k in / 256 out**

| C | out tok/s FI → FlashMLA | TPOT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA | TTFT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 95 → 102 (+7%) | 6.11 → 5.94 | 1128 → 1001 |
| 8 | 257 → 337 (**+31%**) | 20.5 → 14.6 (**−29%**) | 2717 → 2340 |
| 32 | 347 → 414 (**+19%**) | 74.4 → 62.4 (−16%) | 4552 → 3782 |

**Short context: 1k in / 128 out**

| C | out tok/s FI → FlashMLA | TPOT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA | TTFT mean (ms) FI → FlashMLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 144 → 146 | 6.05 → 5.92 | 123 → 122 |
| 8 | 685 → 706 (+3%) | 9.09 → 8.67 | 340 → 349 |
| 32 | 1241 → 973 (−22%) | 21.8 → 24.9 | 518 → 1039 |

**KV capacity:** 3.63M tokens with FI vs 2.83M with FlashMLA. The ratio is 1.28, which is the 512B vs 656B row size.

**Trade-off:**
- FlashMLA wins long-context decode.
- FI holds 28% more tokens and does better on short prompts at high concurrency. The C=32 short-prompt gap is most likely prefill; it is not profiled yet.
- The numbers above are single runs.

## Test Plan / Results (H100)

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashmla_nope_sm90_backend_selection.py`: 34 passed.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k decode_correctness`: 168 passed, 1176 skipped. This includes the new `glm53_flash_nope` case on `fp8_ds_mla` and the DeepSeek regression cases.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k ds_mla`: 3 passed, 5 skipped. The skips are for other architectures or nvfp4.
- `pre-commit` passes, including mypy.
- **Accuracy:** GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8, MTP with 5 spec tokens, GSM8K 5-shot on all 1319 questions.

  | kv cache | backend | GSM8K |
  |---|---|---|
  | fp8_ds_mla (this PR) | FLASHMLA_SPARSE | 0.918 |
  | fp8 (+ #55222 fix) | FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 | 0.913 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix Mamba page size AssertionError with spec decoding on GraniteMoeHybrid, FalconH1 and Zamba2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This fixes the `AssertionError` in `MambaSpec.page_size_bytes` that stops the engine at startup. It happens when `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM` (for example `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny`) runs with speculative decoding and `num_speculative_tokens=2`. The config-time Mamba state shape now counts the speculative tokens, the same way the layer does. `FalconH1ForCausalLM` and `Zamba2ForCausalLM` had the same one-line gap and get the same fix.

Fixes #57721

## Claims

- `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` with ngram speculative decoding and `num_speculative_tokens=2` now starts. Before this fix, it failed during KV cache setup with `AssertionError` at `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:1075`.
- `GraniteMoeHybridForCausalLM`, `FalconH1ForCausalLM` and `Zamba2ForCausalLM` now pass `num_spec=vllm_config.num_speculative_tokens` in `get_mamba_state_shape_from_config`. `Mamba2ForCausalLM` and `NemotronHForCausalLM` already do this.
- A new unit test checks the config-time shape of these three models when speculative tokens are set.

## Validation

Setup: 1 × NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3. vLLM at commit `18f8f96025b556071eb627076f94df560fbd3a22` (`0.30.1rc1.dev630+g18f8f9602`), editable install. This PR is one commit on top of that commit.

Reproducer (`repro.py`), from the issue:

```python
from vllm import LLM
print('=== Starting LLM with num_speculative_tokens=2 ===')
llm = LLM(
    model='ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny',
    max_model_len=4096,
    speculative_config={
        'method': 'ngram',
        'num_speculative_tokens': 2,
        'prompt_lookup_max': 4,
        'prompt_lookup_min': 2,
    },
)
print('=== LLM started successfully ===')
```

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 python repro.py
```

| Tree | Runs | `AssertionError` | Engine started | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `18f8f96` (before) | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| this PR (after) | 2 | 0 | 2 |

The same crash also happens with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit.

Before:

```
(EngineCore pid=217923) INFO 10-04 21:20:48 [interface.py:970] Setting attention block size to 400 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
(EngineCore pid=217923) INFO 10-04 21:20:48 [interface.py:994] Padding mamba page size by 1.59% to ensure that mamba page size and attention page size are exactly equal.
...
  File ".../vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py", line 1075, in page_size_bytes
    assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size
AssertionError
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

After (exit code 0):

```
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:36:57 [interface.py:970] Setting attention block size to 416 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size.
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:36:57 [interface.py:994] Padding mamba page size by 3.94% to ensure that mamba page size and attention page size are exactly equal.
(EngineCore pid=225256) INFO 10-04 21:37:28 [core.py:373] init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 31.43 s (compilation: 0.61 s)
=== LLM started successfully ===
```

Unit test: `test_mamba2_config_state_shape_includes_speculative_tokens` in `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends_selection.py`.

- With the fix: 3 passed.
- With the three model lines reverted: 3 failed, each with `assert ((3, 288), (8, 32, 16)) == ((5, 288), (8, 32, 16))`.

The test was run with `--noconftest`, because the local env had no `tblib` and could not load `tests/conftest.py`. The test uses no fixtures. `pre-commit run --files` passes on the four changed files, including `mypy` and the check that new tests are wired into Buildkite CI.

## Details

Root cause: vLLM plans the Mamba page size at config time and checks it against the real page at runtime. For these models, the planned page and the real page used different conv state shapes.

- `Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`) sizes the padded Mamba page from `get_mamba_state_shape_from_config`. That function did not pass `num_spec`, so the planned conv state for granite-4.0-h-tiny was `(3, 3328)`.
- At runtime, each `MambaMixer2` layer builds its spec from `get_state_shape()`, and that function does pass `num_spec`. So the real conv state is `(5, 3328)`.
- The real page is 13312 bytes bigger than the planned page (3328 × 2 tokens × 2 bytes). Rounding up the attention block size only leaves 12800 bytes of slack. So the real page (819712 bytes) is bigger than the padded page (819200 bytes), and `assert self.page_size_padded >= page_size` fails. With 1 speculative token the gap is only 6656 bytes and fits in the slack. This is why the crash starts at 2 tokens.

Temporary debug prints of the planned shape and the real shape confirmed this. They also showed that the padding arithmetic was correct for the shape it was given: 400 × 2048 = 819200 ≥ 806400. The prints are not in this PR.

#33726 added `num_spec` to `MambaMixer2.get_state_shape` and to the config-time shapes of `Mamba2ForCausalLM` and `NemotronHForCausalLM`. It did not add it to the other three models that use `MambaMixer2`. Only these five models use `MambaMixer2`, so with this PR all five plan the same shape that the layer builds. The assert, the padding logic and the layer are not changed. Now the planner sees the real page size, so it picks an attention block size of 416 tokens (3.94% Mamba padding) instead of 400 tokens (1.59%).

Limitations:

- FalconH1 and Zamba2 get the same one-line fix, but only the unit test checks them. They were not run end to end.
- The reproducer only starts the engine. No generation was run.
- The config-time shape in `vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2.py` does not pass `num_spec`, but `ShortConv.get_state_shape` does. This may be the same kind of mismatch. It is outside this PR and was not tested.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose Fixes #49106. Supersedes #49110. NemotronH is non-gated and passes an empty up-projection name, so the fused-checkpoint name lookup in `build_expert_params_mapping` logged `Unexpected gate/up projection names` for every MoE layer. The warning hid a real bug: on lookup failure the whole fused mapping was dropped, so a NemotronH checkpoint in transformers' native stacked layout (`experts.up_proj` as `[E, I, H]`, written by `save_pretrained(..., save_original_format=False)`) loaded without error and produced garbage. - Mapping and loader branch on `moe_config.is_act_and_mul`. Non-gated layers get a single-shard `up_proj` fused entry plus `down_proj`, and the loader no longer halves w13 for them. The warning is only reachable for gated layers. - The up-projection checkpoint name is `str | None`, checked against the activation in the `RoutedExperts` constructor. NemotronH passes `None`, and the LoRA `..` workaround for the old empty-name entry is removed. Not a duplicate of #49110: that PR only silences the log line and leaves the stacked checkpoint unloadable. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/lora/test_lora_weights.py -v ``` Three new tests cover the non-gated mapping, the unsplit stacked load, and the warning still firing for gated layers. Black-box smoke test: greedy decoding on 4 prompts, 32 tokens, comparing the merge base against this branch for gated and non-gated models, stacked and per-expert checkpoints, with and without LoRA. Scripts are in the details section below. ## Test Result Unit tests: 88 passed. Smoke test, all exact string matches unless noted: | Model | Checkpoint | LoRA | Merge base vs branch | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (gated) | per-expert | – | MATCH, under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | | Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct (gated) | stacked `gate_up_proj` | – | MATCH | | Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 | per-expert | – | MATCH | | Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 | per-expert | zero-init expert adapter | MATCH | | Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 | per-expert | random expert adapter | MATCH | Branch-only checks on the fix itself: | Check | Result | |---|---| | Stacked Nano checkpoint == hub checkpoint | MATCH (on the merge base it loads silently and generates garbage) | | Stacked Nano + zero adapter == per-expert Nano + zero adapter | MATCH | | Zero adapter == LoRA engine with no adapter | 1 token differs on 1/4 prompts after 137 identical chars | | No `Unexpected gate/up projection names` in any branch log | confirmed; every merge-base Nano log has it | Noise baseline: running the unchanged branch twice diverges late (after 43–131 chars) on 3/4 prompts for Qwen3-VL and 2/4 for Nano, so the exact matches above are stronger than the harness guarantees, and the one-token LoRA difference is inside run-to-run noise. NemotronH does not support batch-invariant kernels, and enabling them for Qwen3-VL-MoE produces garbage on both sides, so only the Qwen3 text model ran with deterministic kernels. Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); all changes reviewed and tests run by the submitter.
How the merge-base side was run The "merge base" arms run the same checkout with the five production files this PR changed swapped for their merge-base versions, via a `sitecustomize.py` import hook on `PYTHONPATH`. This isolates exactly the PR's effect with no drift from unrelated commits. Each merge-base log is checked to confirm `routed_experts` was imported from the shadow directory.

do git cat-file -e "$BASE:$f" 2>/dev/null || continue mkdir -p "$SHADOW/$(dirname "$f")" git show "$BASE:$f" > "$SHADOW/$f" echo " $f" done cat > "$SHADOW/sitecustomize.py" <<'EOF' import importlib.util import os import sys SHADOW = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) MODULES = {} for root, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(SHADOW, "vllm")): for name in files: if name.endswith(".py"): path = os.path.join(root, name) rel = os.path.relpath(path, SHADOW)[: -len(".py")] MODULES[rel.replace(os.sep, ".")] = path class ShadowFinder: @staticmethod def find_spec(fullname, path=None, target=None): if fullname not in MODULES: return None return importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(fullname, MODULES[fullname]) sys.meta_path.insert(0, ShadowFinder()) print(f"[shadow] {len(MODULES)} modules overridden from {SHADOW}", file=sys.stderr) EOF # launch : runs one arm, skipping it if its JSON exists. launch() { local name=$1 json=$OUT/$1.json log=$OUT/$1.log shift echo "=== $name" if [ -f "$json" ]; then grep -q "routed_experts from: $(cd "$SHADOW" && pwd)" "$OUT/${tag}_main.log" \ || { echo "shadow did not take effect for $tag"; exit 1; } fi } # Gated, per-expert: A/B against merge-base with deterministic kernels, so the # comparison is exact. Only this model has a batch-invariant MoE path. VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 run qwen_text_per_expert --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 # Gated, stacked: A/B without deterministic kernels (batch-invariant mode breaks # this model), plus a branch repeat to measure run-to-run noise. run qwen_vl_stacked --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct run_branch qwen_vl_stacked_repeat --model Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct # Non-gated, per-expert checkpoint: A/B, with and without LoRA, plus a branch # repeat for the noise baseline (NemotronH does not support batch invariance). run nano_base --model "$NANO" run_branch nano_base_repeat --model "$NANO" run nano_zeros --model "$NANO" --lora "$ZEROS_LORA" run nano_dummy --model "$NANO" --lora "$DUMMY_LORA" # LoRA kernel path with no adapter: the reference for the zero-adapter no-op checks. run_branch nano_lora_noadapter --model "$NANO" --lora-enabled-no-adapter # Non-gated, stacked checkpoint: branch only (merge-base loads it as garbage). if [ -d "$STACKED" ]; then run_branch nano_stacked --model "$STACKED" --tokenizer "$NANO" run_branch nano_stacked_zeros --model "$STACKED" --tokenizer "$NANO" --lora "$ZEROS_LORA" else echo "skipping stacked Nano rows: $STACKED not found (set STACKED=...)" fi echo echo "=== results" $PY summarize_results.py --dir "$OUT" ```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Honor --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers in QSA attention
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`Qwen4ExpQSAAttention` takes its KV cache dtype straight from `cache_config.cache_dtype`, so
`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` is silently ignored on every Qwen4Exp full-attention layer, the MTP
draft layer included. This resolves the dtype per layer, the same way `Attention` and `MLAAttention`
already do (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/{attention,mla_attention}.py`).

Why it matters: with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, FP8 KV in the MTP layer's own attention lowers draft
acceptance at depth on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. Skipping just that layer (`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48`)
keeps the target KV in FP8 and restores acceptance.

## Evidence

DGX Spark (GB10), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 @ada4da32, MTP with 6 drafts, greedy, 41 prompts,
c=1, one node, with this change applied (measured on a nightly 0cbac6cd1-based image; the change is the same two lines on current main):

| target KV | MTP-layer KV | AL | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| fp8 | fp8 | 3.215 | 43.3 |
| bf16 | fp8 | 3.178 | 43.7 |
| fp8 | bf16 (`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48`) | 3.473 | 48.7 |
| bf16 | bf16 | 3.504 | 50.0 |

With FP8 KV in the MTP layer, conditional acceptance at depth 2 to 6 is 0.66 to 0.72. With BF16 it
is 0.74 to 0.80. Depth 1 is unchanged.

At 32k context (8 prompts of 32,928 tokens, 6 GiB KV), the skip costs 7% of the KV pool
(211,502 to 196,608 tokens at 3 drafts). Converting the whole cache to BF16 costs 29%.

## Duplicate check

- PRs and issues searched: "kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers", "kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers",
  "Qwen4Exp kv cache dtype", "QSA fp8 KV", "MTP fp8 kv cache acceptance", and open PRs touching
  qsa.py. None changes how QSA picks its per-layer KV dtype.
- Related, but not overlapping:
  - #54846: fp8/nvfp4 KV read path for QSA.
  - #56116: ModelOpt layer-wise mixed KV.
  - #47618: v1/v2 runner dtype sync.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k skip_layers`
  - New regression test: the MTP layer prefix resolves to `auto` when listed, and stays `fp8` otherwise.
- End to end on GB10 as in the table above (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 48`).

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py` on this branch (rebased on main 042ab0305c): 18 passed, 56 skipped (GPU-only cases).
- pre-commit clean.

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitter reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Keep the HC up projection on the skinny GEMM path
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The SM121 `(10240, 320)` skinny-GEMM plan for the Qwen4Exp HC up projection never runs. The fused HC down projection returns its LoRA activations as a column slice, and the Qwen4Exp dispatch only accepts packed row-major inputs, so every HC up call falls back to cuBLAS. This PR lets the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM take row-major column slices, which its kernel already supports.

## Claims

- On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 on DGX Spark, the HC up projection is the only BF16 GEMM still on cuBLAS during decode: about 101 calls per decode step at 31.6 us each, **3.2 ms per step** (torch profiler on a main-based build, 446 MTP decode steps, c=1). With this PR those calls use the planned skinny kernel. The GEMM is bandwidth bound (6.5 MB of weight per call), so the expected saving is the per-call delta, about 0.8 ms per step (~1%), not the full 3.2 ms.
- Kernel on the real producer layout (column slice of the 336-wide down+inject output): **1.17x to 1.23x** faster than cuBLAS at M=1 to 8, bit-exact against the same kernel on a packed copy.
- No behavior change for packed inputs or other callers (Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.2 keep their own guards).

## Validation

HC up projection, N=10240, K=320, `x = out[:, :320]` with `out` of shape `[M, 336]` (stride `(336, 1)`), DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), CUDA graph, cold L2, CUDA event timing, median of 50 replays:

```
 M   cuBLAS on slice (main)   skinny on slice (PR)   speedup   matches skinny on packed copy
 1   28.8 us                  23.6 us                1.22x     bit-exact
 2   29.1 us                  23.8 us                1.23x     bit-exact
 4   29.1 us                  24.8 us                1.17x     bit-exact
 8   28.7 us                  24.5 us                1.17x     bit-exact
```

Tests on DGX Spark (SM121): `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k qwen4_exp` passes (61 passed, the rest skip on other architectures). A direct check confirms the 336-wide column slice now dispatches to the skinny kernel at M=1, 4, 8 (cosine 1.0 vs `F.linear`) and that a non-row-major `a` is still rejected.

End-to-end, same Spark node, Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP-4, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, c=1, 20 requests, one run per arm:

```
           decode tok/s/user   AL      tok/s per unit AL
main       46.55               2.959   15.73
PR         46.42               2.983   15.56
```

The expected ~1% is within run-to-run noise at c=1, so this PR does not claim an end-to-end speedup; it fixes a dispatch path that silently skips the planned kernel.

## Details

Root cause: `hc_down_silu` returns `output[:, :rank], output[:, rank : rank + hc]`, so the LoRA tensor fed to `input_mix_weight_up` has row stride `rank + hc + pad` (336 for Flash-Next). `_runtime_ok` required `stride == (K, 1)` and rejected it at every M, including M=1. The non-fused path (`split` of the merged projection) produces the same layout.

The skinny kernel is compiled with `make_fake_tensor`, which marks only K as unit stride and leaves the row stride dynamic, and it indexes A through its CuTe layout. Only the Python guards required contiguity. The change:

- `ShapeDynamicSkinnyGemm.__call__` no longer requires `a.is_contiguous()`; `row_stride_ok` requires `a.stride(1) == 1` and checks that the row stride and base pointer keep the `vector_width` loads aligned. Both the kernel entry point and the Qwen4Exp dispatch use it, so an unaligned slice falls back to `F.linear` instead of raising.
- The weight must still be packed.

Same class of silent fallback as #53109 (packed outputs so the Kimi-K3 `q_b_proj` keeps its fast path) and #54565 (row-strided inputs for the DSV3 GEMM).

Not in this PR: Qwen4Exp plans only cover M in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}. Speculative decoding verify widths that are not padded to a planned size (for example M=5 with MTP-4 and default capture sizes) also fall back to cuBLAS. That needs plan or warmup changes and is left for a follow-up.

Duplicate check: the open Qwen4Exp skinny PRs (#59632, #59869, #57848) only edit plan tables, not the input guards.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Count heartbeats as remote engine activity
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`_send_heartbeats` does not stamp `_engine_last_active`, so a decode instance that holds requests waiting on a prefill engine evicts that engine once `engine_ttl` passes, and the same heartbeat starts a new handshake that reloads every remote agent. This stamps the engine when a heartbeat is sent to it.

Fixes #59871

## Claims

- An engine that this instance is heartbeating is no longer evicted by `_evict_stale_engines`, so heartbeats stop causing an evict-and-handshake cycle every `engine_ttl`.
- Engines with no reads and no heartbeats are still evicted after `engine_ttl`, unchanged.

## Validation

New test `test_heartbeated_engine_is_not_evicted` sends a heartbeat every 5 s for twice the TTL with no reads, and checks that the engine stays registered, no remote agent is removed and no handshake is submitted.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_heartbeated_engine_is_not_evicted
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `1 failed`: `AssertionError: assert 'remote-engine-1' in defaultdict(<class 'dict'>, {})` |
| this PR | `1 passed` |

NIXL unit files (`test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_nixl_heartbeat.py`, `test_nixl_push_connector.py`, `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`, `test_handshake_pp_aggregation.py`, `test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry.py`):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `3 failed, 609 passed` |
| this PR | `3 failed, 610 passed` |

The 3 failures are the same on both and come from the CPU-only test machine: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]` and `[None]` (no `torch.ops._C.init_cpu_memory_env`, no Ray on CPU) and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` (gated model, run with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`). Runs were on macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and the manual-stage `mypy-3.12` hook pass.

End-to-end on GPUs. Rig: upstream `main` CI image for `5f30fc7031` (`0.30.1rc1.dev619+g5f30fc703`), NIXL 1.4.1 installed as CI does, bundled UCX 1.22.0, `UCX_TLS=rc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc` over 8 ConnectX RoCE HCAs per node, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B TP1, prefill engines on one H100 node and the decode on another. The change is applied as an overlay of the installed package. Decode with `engine_ttl: 60` and `--max-num-seqs 1`; a 14,000-token request from prefill 2 holds the decode while a request from prefill 1 waits behind it for about 150 s:

| | Handshakes on the decode while the request waits | Decode EngineCore `VmPin` | Requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 2 -> 3 -> 4 (prefill 1 evicted and re-handshaked every ~62 s) | +2,560 KiB per re-handshake | both complete |
| this PR | 2 -> 2 | flat | both complete |

Accuracy, `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_accuracy.py` (gsm8k, P/D through `toy_proxy_server.py`, expected 0.41): `main` 0.4147, this change together with the other two NIXL fixes from the same investigation 0.4139. Both pass.

## Details

Root cause: `_engine_last_active` is stamped at handshake completion (`base_worker.py:1336` on `main`) and when a read is issued (`pull_worker.py:156`). A request queued on the decode side is heartbeated from `on_new_request` until `finished_recving` or abort, and it issues no read until it is scheduled. When `engine_ttl` passes, the heartbeat's `_ensure_handshake` call runs `_evict_stale_engines` first, evicts the engine it is about to heartbeat, finds it missing and submits a handshake.

Why it matters: each reload runs `remove_remote_agent` and `loadRemoteMD` for every remote rank. On a deployment with TP2 decode and PCP8 prefill (8 remote agents per engine per worker), each full re-handshake left 476-481 64 KiB UCX buffers (about 960 VMAs) per worker, which is a separate NIXL/UCX issue. A decode rank that could not admit work kept requests waiting for tens of minutes at a time. It ran about 6 handshakes per hour against about 1 per hour on healthy ranks, and it hit `vm.max_map_count` after about 31 hours. This change removes the heartbeat-driven part of that churn. An engine that is idle with nothing waiting on it is still evicted, and it is handshaked again when new work arrives, which is the intended TTL behavior.

The stamp sits after the pending-handshake `continue`, so it runs only when `_ensure_handshake` returned `None`, which means the engine is in `_remote_agents`. That keeps the invariant #52245 relies on: no `_engine_last_active` entry without a `_remote_agents` entry, since `_cleanup_remote_engine` asserts it.

Tradeoff: a dead prefill engine stays registered while requests still wait on it. Those requests fail their reads, which stops the heartbeat, and #50047 releases a replaced peer without waiting for the TTL.

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR or issue matched `nixl heartbeat`, `engine_ttl`, `engine ttl evict`, `nixl heartbeat engine_ttl`, `engine_ttl heartbeat`, `stale remote engine` or `nixl re-handshake` for this mechanism. Closest precedents are #52245 (same stamp for the push-mode D side) and #54689 (eviction skips engines with in-flight reads).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Keep batch x heads out of gridDim.z in the GLM-5.3-Flash fused recurrent KDA kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a start-up crash of GLM-5.3-Flash in data-parallel deployments (TP=1 per rank): `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` was launched with `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)`, and with 64 KDA value heads on one GPU the first CUDA-graph capture batch of 1024 sequences needs `1024 * 64 = 65536` programs — one over the CUDA `gridDim.z` limit of 65535 — so the launch fails with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument` and `--data-parallel-size 4` (with or without EP) cannot start. TP4 (16 heads per rank) is unaffected.

The kernel now carries `N * HV` in `gridDim.x` (limit 2^31-1) with the `program_id` mapping swapped accordingly. Scope (narrowed in review): only the NVIDIA GLM-5.3-Flash copy under `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/` (`kernels.py`, `fused_recurrent.py`) and its test are changed. The same `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` pattern exists in the AMD GLM copy and in `third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/{fused_recurrent,fused_sigmoid_gating,kda}.py`; those are intentionally left unchanged here (no AMD reproduction available; the shared kernels serve other models and need their own validation) and are candidates for separate follow-up. The packed-decode kernel in the same GLM file already guarded this case (`split_batch_head_grid = B * HV > 65535`). The narrowed change serves every GLM-5.3-Flash TP configuration; the failure itself needs TP=1 per rank (DP) at the default capture sizes.

Fixes #56973

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched vllm-project/vllm open and closed PRs and issues (GitHub search, 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-15) for `fused_recurrent_kda`, `gridDim.z`, `65535`, `invalid argument` + GLM-5.3-Flash / KDA / DP: no report of this crash and no PR touching the launch grid of `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel`; the only related guard is the existing `split_batch_head_grid` check in the packed-decode kernel of the same file.

## Test Plan

- Regression case added to the existing `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (`test_fused_recurrent_kda_more_than_65535_programs`, parametrized 1024×64 and 2048×48 (sequence, head) programs with head dim 16): the full batch must be bitwise identical to the same batch run in two halves. It fails on the unpatched kernel with the Triton launch error and passes with this change.
- Existing test that exercises the changed kernel: `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (NVIDIA glm5next `fused_recurrent_kda`). The flash-linear-attention and AMD copies are no longer touched by this PR.

## Test commands run and results

On 4× GB200 (SM100), 2026-09-11 nightly image, the changed kernel files mounted over the installed package (`/tmp/t` holds a copy of `tests/` so `import vllm` resolves to the installed package):

```
pip install tblib
python3 -m pytest -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py
python3 -m pytest -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py \
    tests/kernels/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py \
    tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py
```

- `test_kda_recurrent.py` with the new case: stock kernel — 2 failed (the two new parametrizations, `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`), 6 passed; patched kernel — 8 passed.
- The six files (before the new case was added): 197 passed / 7 skipped on stock, 197 passed / 7 skipped with the fix.
- Bitwise equivalence stock vs patched on identical inputs (plain-decode calls at 16, 1024, 4096 and 64000 programs; spec-decode-style calls with 2-D state indices and `num_accepted_tokens` at T=4 and T=6): outputs and state updates `torch.equal`; both deterministic run to run. On the crashing shape (1024 × 64) the patched output equals a reference assembled from two stock half-batches, bitwise.
- End to end: `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel` starts, captures its graphs and serves an 8k-in/1k-out sweep at concurrency 1–128; TP4 with the patch reproduces stock TP4 throughput (169.6 vs 169.1 tok/s at c=1, 1898.6 vs 1897.4 at c=32); gsm8k 5-shot greedy on the patched DP4+EP server 0.927 vs 0.934 for stock TP4 (paired exact McNemar p = 0.29 on the 57 discordant questions).
- 2026-09-21, after narrowing — kernel regression test only (the TP4 / DP4+EP serving runs and the gsm8k evaluation above were done before the narrowing and were not repeated, since the NVIDIA GLM kernel files are unchanged by it): same image and procedure, with only the two NVIDIA GLM kernel files copied over the installed package; the three shared flash-linear-attention wrappers were left as installed (their `grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)` lines checked present by grep). Stock: 2 failed / 6 passed in `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py` (the two > 65535-program cases, `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`); with the two files: 8 passed.

## Model evaluation

gsm8k, lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13, 5-shot, greedy, one prompt per request, all 1319 questions: patched DP4 + EP server 0.927 (1223 correct) vs stock TP4 0.934 (1232 correct); paired exact McNemar on the 57 discordant questions p = 0.29 (no detectable difference; the kernel outputs themselves are bitwise identical to stock where stock can run).

commits.pr_title: [Model][DeepSeek-V4] Make MegaMoE shared-expert finalize independent of linear post-load order
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

MegaMoE fuses the DeepSeek-V4 shared expert using the shared linears' block-FP8 UE8M0 scales. Those linears' own DeepGEMM post-load hook repacks the same scales into int32, in place.

`_finalize_shared_expert_weights` only converted scales that were still in checkpoint layout, and passed packed scales straight to MegaMoE. So it was only correct when it ran **before** that hook:
- Real loads finalize inside `load_weights`, before the hook, so they are fine.
- A dummy load never calls `load_weights` and finalizes **after** the hook. With DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MegaMoE + EP, DeepGEMM then asserts at startup (`layout.hpp:114`).

The packed layout already stores one UE8M0 byte per (row, k-block), four k-blocks per int32. `_prepare_shared_expert_scale` now reads per-row exponents from either layout and builds the same 1x32 MegaMoE scale. The rest of the path is unchanged, including the existing shape check and the fallback to the serial shared MLP.

This removes the ordering constraint that keeps DeepSeek-V4 finalizing inside `load_weights`. #57733 builds on it.

## Test Plan / Results

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py::test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe_finalizes_native_shared_expert_weights` gains two `-packed` cases. Their scales are packed by the real linear-hook packer (`deepgemm_post_process_weight_scale_block`) before finalize runs. Results on GB200:
- With this PR: 7 passed.
- On `main`: both `-packed` cases fail at the check that the scale reaching MegaMoE equals the checkpoint scale.
- The rest of the file has 14 failures, identical on `main`. They are V4.1 / hash-routing tests that need a DeepGEMM build with `bf16_mega_gate`.

GPU checks with real DeepGEMM. Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this commit, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

| check | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Fused shared scale from checkpoint scales vs from hook-packed scales. Shapes (4096, 4096), (4096, 2048), (6144, 7168), (7168, 3072). | packed scales not converted | **bitwise identical** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4-layer config (FP4 experts), MegaMoE + EP, TP1, `load_format="dummy"` | startup crash, DeepGEMM `layout.hpp:114` | starts; shared expert **fused** on all 4 layers; finite logprobs |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, real weights, `vllm serve` DP4 / EP4, MegaMoE (shared expert fused); greedy decoding, top-5 logprobs | baseline | **bit-identical** tokens and logprobs, 4/4 prompts |

`pre-commit` passes.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `MegaMoE shared expert`, `_finalize_shared_expert_weights`, `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` and `deepseek v4 dummy load mega moe`. None of them changes how the shared-expert scales are read.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Merge QSA QKVG and indexer QK projections
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**Projection fusion.** Merge Qwen4Exp QSA’s QKVG and replicated indexer Q/K projections into **one GEMM**. LoRA keeps separate projections with standard linear dispatch.

**GEMM dispatch.** LL-GEMM for merged GEMM

- SM103 (GB300): TP4 shape, done by me
- SM100 (B200): TP4 contributed by @namgyu-youn
- SM90 (H200): TP4 contributed tuning for M=1/2/4
- SM121 (GB10): TP1 contributed by @stecasta
- Also prune obsolete merged-HC and separate-QSA plans;

**Prepare kernel.** Support strided merged outputs and widen row-offset arithmetic to i64, with **no noticeable performance difference** in GB300 checks (≤1% in repeat measurements).

## Validation

### Microbenchmark

One GB300, BF16, TP=4: `X=[M,2560]`, separate weights `[3584,2560]` + `[640,2560]`, merged weight `[4224,2560]`. Both arms use production `qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm`: LL-GEMM at M=1/4, cuBLAS via standard linear at M>=16. The separate arm times both GEMMs without concatenation, using the original dispatch table from `9e6550bd05`; the reproduction restores that table for the baseline after pruning.

FlashInfer CUPTI, CUDA graphs, cold L2; median of three runs × 50 iterations, alternating arm order. Correctness checked against FP32 accumulation (`rtol=0.02`, `atol=0.01`). Torch `2.13.0+cu130`, baseline `9e6550bd05`.

| M | Separate (µs) | Merged (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 9.857 | 6.624 | 1.49x |
| 4 | 11.024 | 7.616 | 1.45x |
| 16 | 13.472 | 8.032 | 1.68x |
| 64 | 13.664 | 8.224 | 1.66x |
| 256 | 13.584 | 9.216 | 1.47x |
| 1024 | 21.920 | 15.584 | 1.41x |
| 4096 | 51.809 | 51.648 | 1.00x |
| 16384 | 191.424 | 185.233 | 1.03x |

Largest spread between run medians: 5.5%. These measure projection GEMMs only; M=4096 is effectively neutral.

<details>
<summary>Microbenchmark reproduction</summary>

Run in a vLLM CUDA development venv with matching FlashInfer and `cupti-python` installed. Save the following script as `workspace/benchmark_qsa_projection_dispatch.py`, then run:

```bash
mkdir -p workspace
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 .venv/bin/python workspace/benchmark_qsa_projection_dispatch.py
```

```python
import ast
import dataclasses
import json
import statistics
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia import low_latency_gemm as dispatch

M_VALUES = (1, 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384)
ROUNDS = 3
REPEAT_ITERS = 50
BASELINE_COMMIT = "9e6550bd058560bec5690b6c06474adf048a9b85"


def baseline_plans():
    source = subprocess.check_output([
        "git", "show",
        f"{BASELINE_COMMIT}:vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py",
    ], text=True)
    node = next(node for node in ast.parse(source).body
                if isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign)
                and node.target.id == "QWEN4_EXP_GEMM_PLANS")
    namespace = {"SkinnyGemmConfig": dispatch.SkinnyGemmConfig}
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[node], type_ignores=[]), "baseline-plans", "exec"), namespace)
    return namespace["QWEN4_EXP_GEMM_PLANS"]


def timing(fn, cold):
    samples = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
        fn, dry_run_iters=5, repeat_iters=REPEAT_ITERS,
        use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=cold,
    )
    return statistics.median(samples) * 1000


def main():
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    weight = torch.randn(4224, 2560, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02
    qkv_weight, index_weight = weight.split((3584, 640), dim=0)
    real_skinny = dispatch.shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm
    records = []
    def spy(x, w, config):
        records.append((tuple(w.shape), dataclasses.asdict(config)))
        return real_skinny(x, w, config)
    results = {
        'gpu': torch.cuda.get_device_name(), 'torch': torch.__version__,
        'baseline_commit': BASELINE_COMMIT,
        'candidate_commit': subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], text=True).strip(),
        'dtype': 'bf16', 'tp': 4, 'k': 2560, 'separate_n': [3584, 640],
        'merged_n': 4224, 'm_values': M_VALUES, 'rounds': ROUNDS,
        'iterations_per_round': REPEAT_ITERS, 'cuda_graph': True, 'results': [],
    }
    old_plans = baseline_plans()
    capability = dispatch.current_platform.get_device_capability()
    merged_plans = dispatch.QWEN4_EXP_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY.get(capability, {})
    op = torch.ops.vllm.qwen4_exp_low_latency_gemm
    for m in M_VALUES:
        x = torch.randn(m, 2560, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        def separate():
            with patch.dict(dispatch.QWEN4_EXP_GEMM_PLANS_BY_CAPABILITY, {capability: old_plans}):
                return op(x, qkv_weight), op(x, index_weight)
        def merged():
            return op(x, weight)
        arms = {'separate': separate, 'merged': merged}
        row = {'m': m, 'dispatch': {}}
        for name, fn in arms.items():
            records.clear()
            with patch.object(dispatch, 'shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm', side_effect=spy):
                output = fn()
            row['dispatch'][name] = list(records)
            sizes = (3584, 640) if name == 'separate' else (4224,)
            plans = old_plans if name == "separate" else merged_plans
            expected = sum(m in plans.get((n, 2560), {}) for n in sizes)
            assert len(records) == expected, (m, name, expected, records)
            outputs = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else output.split((3584, 640), dim=1)
            for actual, w in zip(outputs, (qkv_weight, index_weight)):
                reference = torch.nn.functional.linear(x.float(), w.float()).bfloat16()
                torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference, rtol=2e-2, atol=1e-2)
            for _ in range(10):
                fn()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        for cold in (True,):
            mode = 'cold' if cold else 'hot'
            times = {name: [] for name in arms}
            for run in range(ROUNDS):
                order = ('separate', 'merged') if run % 2 == 0 else ('merged', 'separate')
                for name in order:
                    times[name].append(timing(arms[name], cold))
            row[mode] = {
                name: {'median_us': statistics.median(ts), 'run_medians_us': ts,
                       'tflops': 2*m*2560*4224 / (statistics.median(ts)*1e6)}
                for name, ts in times.items()
            }
            row[mode]['speedup'] = row[mode]['separate']['median_us'] / row[mode]['merged']['median_us']
        results['results'].append(row)
        Path('workspace/qsa_projection_dispatch_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2)+'\n')
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

</details>

### Local correctness

**16 prepare tests passed before rebase; the focused LL-GEMM suite passed again after rebase: 7 passed, 102 architecture-specific skips.**

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare.py -q --tb=short
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k qwen4_exp -q --tb=short
```

Local checks also passed for BF16/FP8 projections and checkpoint loading across TP=1/2/4/8, LoRA fallback construction, and FP8 per-tensor/block scales. Sparse inputs crossing `2**31` elements verified the widened offsets. Another 36 checks verified standard-linear dispatch for pruned shapes. Capability-map selection and unsupported-capability fallback checks passed; CUDA projection checks at M=1/2/4/16 also passed after dispatch cleanup. Existing Buildkite suites cover QSA prepare/reference and LL-GEMM tests. The contributed H200 merged-GEMM plans passed local table and routing checks; H200 GPU correctness tests were skipped on this host.

### End-to-end performance

**TEP4 + MTP3, 4× GB300**, Qwen4Exp BF16. Baseline `aee8fe202a` (validation baseline) → feature `401b1249c0`, run sequentially on the same node with matched dependencies. Existing SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k` workload: inputs capped at 8192 tokens, 1024 output tokens, prefix caching off, five warmups, ten prompts per concurrency slot.

| Concurrency | Output tokens/s, base → feature | Change | Mean TTFT (ms), base → feature | Mean TPOT (ms), base → feature |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 317.0 → 315.7 | -0.4% | 157.8 → 145.6 | 3.003 → 3.028 |
| 4 | 843.0 → 855.6 | +1.5% | 198.6 → 187.6 | 4.358 → 4.322 |
| 16 | 1883.4 → 1934.0 | +2.7% | 335.3 → 260.1 | 7.980 → 7.788 |
| 64 | 3566.3 → 3747.6 | +5.1% | 564.0 → 561.4 | 17.046 → 16.237 |

**0 failed requests** across 850 measured requests per arm. One sweep per arm; no repeated-run variability estimate. Throughput is effectively neutral at concurrency 1 and improves up to 5.1% at concurrency 64. MTP acceptance was 36.56% in both arms at concurrency 64.

### End-to-end accuracy

**Feature only, TEP4 + MTP3**, same BF16 model and node; prefix caching on. GSM8K: 5-shot, two epochs, temperature 0, thinking off, max 1024 tokens, concurrency 32. MMMU-Pro: thinking on, max 65536 tokens, concurrency 64.

| Task | Responses | Flexible score | Strict score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 2638 | 96.55% | 96.63% |
| MMMU-Pro | 1730 | 76.65% | 76.59% |

**0 request errors** for both tasks. Scores are close to historical results (~96.7% GSM8K, 76.94% MMMU-Pro); no contemporaneous baseline accuracy run was requested.

<details>
<summary>End-to-end reproduction</summary>

Serving and performance commands below reproduce the tested configuration. Run each worktree with its independent venv on the same four GPUs, using the same BF16 checkpoint. Accuracy settings are listed above; the original evaluation harness is not included here.

Shared serving environment: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1`. Torch `2.13.0+cu130`, Triton `3.7.1`, FlashInfer `0.7.0.post1`; Python 3.12.13. Source SHAs are recorded from git.

```bash

MODEL=/path/to/qwen4_exp_checkpoint

# Accuracy server, feature only:
.venv/bin/vllm serve "$MODEL" --port 8000 -tp 4 -ep \
  --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Reset SimpleCPU eager-store placement state on MRV2 resume
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

SimpleCPU eager offload retains each request's accumulated GPU block table and
per-group store cursors. Under MRV2, preemption is reported through
`SchedulerOutput.preempted_req_ids`, while the resumed request is represented
as complete `NewRequestData`. Its `yield_req_data` entry is not marked
preempted, so the eager-store state appends the replacement table to the freed
placement and keeps its old cursors. In the regression, the resumed
three-block request therefore schedules no newly confirmed tail block for
offload instead of scheduling the third block.

When preemption is observed, immediately clear the retained block table and
reset every group cursor before processing any placement data from that
scheduler output. MRV1 resumed-cached requests and MRV2 `NewRequestData` then
consume their complete replacement tables through the same reset site.

The change is confined to eager SimpleCPU store bookkeeping. It does not alter
lazy mode, cache lookup, or eviction policy.

#47234 documents current below-cursor CPU-cache eviction behavior, while
#47235 proposes cursor re-scans for that case. This change is narrower: it
restores the existing preemption reset for MRV2's `NewRequestData`
representation and does not change eviction tracking. #57325 touches the
same files but contains no equivalent reset. #55033 also touches the
manager and scheduler tests for non-prefix-cacheable QSA/lazy sizing, but does
not reset retained placement after MRV2 preemption. #57505 guards
hashless sources at store completion; it is downstream of placement tracking
and contains no preemption reset.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with the current-main refresh,
implementation, testing, and drafting. I reviewed the final diff and the test
results.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py::\
test_eager_store_resets_block_cursor_after_preemption
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/simple_kv_offload
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::\
test_cached_request_data_resumed_all_token_ids_mrv1_only \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_kv_connector_handles_preemption \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::\
test_priority_scheduling_preemption_and_resumption_when_out_of_kv
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py
```

## Test Result

On upstream `main` commit
`155488d853a0bc42df227dbfc74005b3fd488e94`, the test-only control gives two
passes and two failures: both MRV1 controls pass, while both MRV2 cases return
no store blocks (`[]`) instead of the resumed tail block (`[5]`). The matrix
covers delayed resumption and same-output preemption/resumption.

With this change:

```text
candidate head:            d30e9cf8d50f
targeted regression:       4 passed
full scheduler test file:  60 passed
SimpleCPU test directory:  95 passed, 2 skipped
adjacent lifecycle matrix: 13 passed
changed-file pre-commit:  passed
manual mypy (Python 3.12): passed
git diff --check:         passed
```

The reviewer-requested simplification removes the deferred reset marker and
the separate MRV1 reset branch. The production code now resets directly from
the scheduler's authoritative `preempted_req_ids` set before consuming either
runner's resumed placement. The runtime scenario and assertions are unchanged.

All runs above were local CPU runs, finalized on 2026-10-04. The fresh

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix Qwen4Exp PLE embedding rejecting INC (AutoRound) checkpoints
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #59798. `Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound` is an AutoRound checkpoint, which vLLM loads as `INCConfig`. It failed at model construction with `NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config INCConfig`. `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod.from_quant_config` now asks `INCConfig` whether the PLE layer is quantized. #59431 does the same for compressed-tensors.

## Claims

- The command from the issue (TP=2, expert parallel) no longer raises. Both workers build the PLE n-gram table with `Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` (bf16), and model construction finishes.
- The checkpoint's own INC metadata makes the choice: its `extra_config` has `".*ple.*": {"bits": 16, "data_type": "float"}`. If INC says the PLE layer is quantized, the old `NotImplementedError` is still raised, because there is no INC-quantized PLE format.
- The branch is in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ngram_embedding.py`, so both the NVIDIA and the AMD Qwen4Exp paths get it.
- A new unit test covers both cases.

## Validation

Hardware: 2 × NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB. Before: commit `18f8f96025b556071eb627076f94df560fbd3a22`. After: this PR on top of that commit.

Reproducer, from the issue. No request is needed, because the crash happens at startup:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel
```

| | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 1 | Both workers raise `NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp PLE embedding does not support quantization config INCConfig` during model construction, before weight loading. The engine exits with code 1. The `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit gives the same error. | | After | 2 | No `NotImplementedError` in either run. Both workers build the PLE table, and model construction finishes (about 56 s). |

After the fix, both workers log:

```
Initialized PLE embedding language_model.model.layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding: quantization_method=Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod, weight_dtype=torch.bfloat16, weight_device=cpu, pinned=True
```

Limitation: neither "after" run reached a ready server. Both runs next stopped at the weight download, with a `PermissionError` from `huggingface_hub`. The HF cache on the test machine had only the config and tokenizer files for this model, and we could not write to it. This happens after the bug site, in code the patch does not touch. The "before" run never got that far. No run here loaded the real weights, and no accuracy eval was run. Before merge, someone with the weights should run the reproducer to a ready server and run an accuracy check.

Extra checks (not the reproducer):

- The same command with `--load-format dummy`: weights loaded (35.44 GiB per GPU), CUDA graphs were captured, and the server became ready. One `/v1/completions` request returned 16 tokens. The text is noise, because the weights are random.
- The checkpoint's safetensors headers on the Hub: the PLE n-gram table is 128 plain BF16 shards (`[2500012, 160]` each), with no `qweight`, `scales` or `qzeros`. This matches the unquantized method.
- Unit tests: `pytest --noconftest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -k "inc_layer_config or rejects_unsupported or modelopt_exclusion or shard_exclusions or mixed_precision"` gives `6 passed, 69 deselected`. `--noconftest` was used because `tests/conftest.py` needs `tblib`, which the test env did not have. With the INC branch turned off in a separate process (tree unchanged), the new test's config gets the old `NotImplementedError` again. So the test catches the bug.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files: every hook passed or was skipped, including ruff and mypy.

## Details

Root cause: `from_quant_config` gets the model-level quantization config. That config describes the model body, which is not always the same as the PLE table. The method could only ask four config families whether the PLE layer is excluded: ModelOpt mixed precision, ModelOpt, compressed-tensors and FP8. Any other config fell through to the `NotImplementedError`. This checkpoint quantizes `model.language_model.layers` to 4 bits, but its `extra_config` marks `.*ple.*` as 16-bit float. `INCConfig` keeps this metadata and resolves it with `config_parser.resolve(layer, prefix)`, but the PLE code never asked it.

How it was found: on the unpatched tree, a debug print just before the raise showed three things. The config was a plain `INCConfig`, with no handled class in its MRO. The prefix was `language_model.model.layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding`. And `resolve(None, prefix)` returned `bits=16, quantized=False`. So the INC metadata is already mapped to vLLM names and matches the prefix. Only the dispatch ignored it.

Fix: one `if` in `from_quant_config`. For an `INCConfig`, when `quant_config.config_parser.resolve(None, prefix).quantized` is false, it returns `Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. `INCConfig.get_quant_method` uses the same `resolve(...).quantized` check for its own layers. Passing `None` as the layer is safe: `_resolve_raw` only uses the layer in `isinstance(layer, ParallelLMHead)` and `layer.__class__.__name__`, and both work with `None`. The compressed-tensors branch also passes `None`. Size: +6 lines in `ngram_embedding.py`, and +19 lines of test in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py`. That test file already runs in Buildkite (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`).

Design choice for review: INC's own `get_quant_method` treats every layer that is not linear or MoE as unquantized, whatever `resolve` says. This patch is stricter. An INC checkpoint that puts the PLE table inside a quantized block, with no 16-bit exclusion, still gets `NotImplementedError`. The new test checks this case on purpose. Please say if you prefer INC's looser behavior.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the compressor ring out of the null block
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`_ring_slot_mapping_kernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/compressor.py`) maps each token to `block_table[req, 0] * capacity + pos % capacity`. Warmup and CUDA-graph capture run dummy batches whose block tables are zeroed, so their compressor state rows are written into **block 0**. That is the null block, and every KV-cache group shares it. The fp32 state bytes therefore land in other layers' pages. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, layer 2's ring overlaps the sliding-window KV of layers 0–13, and layer 8's overlaps layers 0–27.

Why it matters: sparse MLA decode kernels gather the null block for masked candidates and weight it by zero. When the bytes decode to a non-finite value, 0 × NaN is still NaN. On sm_120 (FlashInfer's DSv4 sparse decode) with DSpark speculative decoding and FULL CUDA graphs, this produced wrong outputs on the first request (0 accepted drafts), then `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` / Xid 31 MMU faults on the next prefill.

The bug is latent without DSpark too: block 0 still ends dirty (we measured 29 NaN bytes). It used to be masked because `warmup_kernels` ran after `capture_model`, and that warmup zeroed block 0 again. `gpu_worker.py` now runs `warmup_kernels` before `capture_model`, so the bytes survive into serving.

The fix maps tokens whose ring block is 0 to PAD (`-1`), which the ring consumers already skip. Real requests never own block 0, so their mapping is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- New `test_v41_compressor_ring_never_writes_the_null_block`, next to the existing `test_v41_compressor_metadata_maps_tokens_to_their_ring`: a dummy request on block 0 must map to PAD, and a real request next to it must keep its ring slots.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched files.

## Test Result

- Both tests pass with the fix. As a control, the new test fails without it: `assert [0, 1, 25, 26] == [-1, -1, 25, 26]`, i.e. the dummy tokens are written to slots 0 and 1 of the null block. This ran on an RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120) in the `nightly-e9757321` image with the patched `compressor.py`, using the two test functions verbatim (the full test file imports modules newer than that nightly).
- End-to-end on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8, DSpark (`num_speculative_tokens=5`), FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs, prefix caching, v0.30.0 plus our sm_120 page-geometry patch (needed to serve this model on sm_120 at all, and unrelated to this change):
  - without the fix: block 0 of every sliding-window layer is non-finite after capture, the first request decodes garbage, and the next ~1.6k-token prefill raises Xid 31;
  - with the fix: all 13 block-0 views stay clean through capture and 11,000 decode steps (including c16 load); needle retrieval 9/9, greedy determinism and shared-prefix divergence checks pass; 0 Xid; c1 131 tok/s, c16 672 tok/s, DSpark acceptance 0.38.
- Not verified: an end-to-end run on current `main`, and GPUs other than sm_120.

A related robustness point, arguably for FlashInfer: its SM120 DSv4 sparse decode is only correct while slot 0 is finite, because masked candidates still contribute 0 × V.

AI assistance was used to find this bug and write the patch and test. The tests above were run as described.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][LoRA] Add deterministic split-K=8 LoRA shrink for batch invariance
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the LoRA shrink kernel runs with `SPLIT_K=1`, because split-K normally reduces with float atomics. This PR makes the batch-invariant shrink keep K parallelism without atomics: `_lora_shrink_kernel` stores unscaled FP32 partials for 8 fixed K splits (BLOCK_K=256 for every M) and a small reducer adds them in a fixed order and applies scaling once.

This PR:
- adds a `STORE_PARTIALS` branch to `do_shrink_kernel` / `_lora_shrink_kernel` and a fixed-order reducer, used whenever `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (no new env var);
- allocates the FP32 partials per call with `torch.empty`, so each CUDA graph keeps its scratch in its own pool;
- leaves the non-batch-invariant path unchanged; the split-K path does not use PDL.

Batch-invariant LoRA outputs are still invariant across batch composition, but they change relative to the previous `SPLIT_K=1` path because the reduction order differs.

Not a duplicate: #50278 forces `split_k=1` on the default (non-BI) path; #58533 changes PDL overlap on the dual-stream path.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k batch_invariant` (FP64 reference over K tail / empty split / 3 slices / no-LoRA rows; bitwise-equal target row across M = 31…129)
- `pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k "test_kernels and shrink"` (non-BI path)
- `lm_eval` gsm8k and `vllm bench serve`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, Qwen3-4B + LoRA adapter, requests targeting the adapter, this PR vs main

## Test Result

- `pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k batch_invariant`: 6 passed; `-k "test_kernels and shrink"`: 2136 passed (H100 and B200)

commits.pr_body:

## Overview

The model-not-found 404 now lists the valid names for the served model: ``The model `x` does not exist. Valid aliases: my-model.``

Replaces #58025 (closed when my fork was re-created; same commit, rebased). Related: #59888 (client side of the same confusion).

## Claims

- A request for an unserved model name gets the valid model names in the error message, so the client does not need `/v1/models` or the server log to fix it.
- Status code, `type` and `param` are unchanged.

## Validation

Live server, `--served-model-name qwen3.8-27b`:

```
# before
$ curl -s -XPOST localhost:8000/tokenize -d '{"model":"not-a-served-model","prompt":"x"}'
{"error":{"message":"The model `not-a-served-model` does not exist.","type":"NotFoundError","param":"model","code":404}}

{"error":{"message":"The model `not-a-served-model` does not exist. Served models: qwen3.8-27b.","type":"NotFoundError","param":"model","code":404}}
```

Validated on v0.28.0; the diff applies unchanged to current `main`. `pre-commit` passes. No test added: this is a message-text change. I can pin it in `tests/entrypoints/` if you want.

**Motivation.** `--served-model-name` makes the served name differ from `--model`, and clients that send the checkpoint path get a 404 that reads like a missing route. `self.models.base_model_paths` already holds the list that `/v1/models` publishes, so no new data is exposed.

**Scope.** Base models only; loaded LoRA adapter names are not listed, to keep the message short.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Determinism] Preserve output dtype in batch-invariant mean
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59078. In batch-invariant mode, `mean_batch_invariant` returns FP32 for FP16/BF16 inputs when no output dtype is requested. This promotes DeepEncoder's `LayerNorm2d` output to FP32, causing the next BF16 convolution to fail during startup.

Restore the input dtype at the final return while retaining FP32 accumulation and the existing reduction order. Explicit FP32 requests remain FP32. Extend the existing determinism suite with default/explicit output dtype coverage across FP16/BF16/FP32 and single/multiple reduction dimensions.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-28): reviewed #59078 and its comments and searched open PRs for `59078 in:body` and `mean_batch_invariant`. No competing fix or ownership claim was found. Related #55249 fixes softmax and #55466 fixes matmul precision; neither addresses this mean output dtype.
